scope: Targeted programme review and explicit continuation queue. The queue includes unreviewed leads and inherited gap findings, separately labelled; it is not a completed review of all 1,628 candidates.

records.title: Feminist Studies
records.qualification: An interdisciplinary women’s-studies institution with a documented women’s-history component. The edge does not restrict its programme to history or date the origin of women’s history to 1972; organizing began in 1969.

records.title: Signs: Journal of Women in Culture and Society
records.qualification: Links the historical component of a broader feminist scholarly programme. This is neither a claim of exclusive disciplinary affiliation nor an origin date for all women’s history.

records.title: Social Science History
records.qualification: An institutional project within the broad social-history expansion, with qualitative as well as quantitative methods. Its interdisciplinary scope exceeds this atlas entry; it does not endorse every approach listed in the entry.

records.title: The Economic History Review
records.qualification: Consolidates an existing field through a society journal. The programme included social history and cannot be reduced to later cliometrics; 1926 is the society’s foundation, not this first publication date.

records.title: Oral History Review
records.qualification: One institutional forum in a much older and internationally diverse practice. The US association, its newsletter and the separate British journal Oral History are not conflated.

records.title: History in Africa
records.qualification: A specific source-critical programme within African historiography, not the creation of African historical thought or an assignment of every African historian to one method. Claim limited to the available first-editorial extract.

records.title: Gender & History
records.qualification: Retrospective abstract-level evidence supports this limited founding-purpose claim. The target is the gender-history component of the combined Gender & racial formation entry; the edge does not date or subsume every racial-formation approach.

records.title: Journal of Interdisciplinary History
records.qualification: The quantitative connection is one explicit component of a broader founding programme. The journal is not exclusively quantitative and the link does not equate its programme with all cliometric or serial-history approaches.

records.title: Isis
records.qualification: Preserves the existing 1912 foundation date and explicitly distinguishes 1913 first publication. The initial Sartonian synthesis is one programme within history of science; it does not characterize the entire field or the journal’s later pluralism.

records.title: Comparative Studies in Society and History
records.qualification: Its comparative programme offers an institutional home for historical sociology but extends to anthropology and the humanities. The edge neither reduces the journal to sociology nor assigns it the later state-formation theories in this atlas entry.

records.title: Environment and History
records.qualification: An expansion and consolidation project in an already established field. Its explicit geographical ambitions provide evidence against treating North American environmental-history venues as the field’s whole institutional history.

records.title: Nations and Nationalism
records.qualification: A field-consolidating institution after earlier decades of nationalism scholarship, not the field’s beginning or an endorsement of a single explanation of nations.

records.title: Holocaust and Genocide Studies
records.qualification: The edge connects the Holocaust component of a wider programme to the existing atlas entry. Comparative genocide studies is not thereby claimed to be comprehensively represented by that entry; the evidence is contemporary reception, not a full reading of the founding editorial.

records.title: History and Anthropology
records.qualification: A particular institutional exchange, not the origin of historical anthropology. Distinct from Stocking’s History of Anthropology series, which the same contemporary review contrasts with this journal; intended collaboration does not prove that disciplinary divisions disappeared.

records.title: Representations
records.reason: Representations has a relevant editors’ statement, but the accessible statement is undated. Establish its relationship to the 1983 launch before attaching a historical founding edge.

records.title: Journal of the History of Sexuality
records.reason: Journal of the History of Sexuality: John C. Fout’s first-issue Editorial, 1(1), July 1990, pp. 1–2, is identified. Current remit alone does not establish its founding programme.

records.title: History and Theory
records.reason: History and Theory: first volume dates to 1960–61, but read an original programme or explicit institutional history before linking to philosophy of history and filling the absent canonical date.

records.title: Environmental History
records.reason: Environmental History: the 1996 merger is documented; finish the merger programme review. Earlier predecessor dates must not become the current title’s first publication.

records.title: Radical History Review
records.reason: Radical History Review: reconcile the 1973 MARHO newsletter and the journal title before filling the missing start and linking to radical history. Current journal remit is insufficient.

records.title: The Journal of African History
records.reason: The Journal of African History: the 1960 foundation is known, but its initial programme and institutional exclusions need a scoped reading. History in Africa supplies a different, accepted source-critical programme.

records.title: Journal of Economic History
records.reason: Journal of Economic History: retain the checked 1941 start. A search located a 1951 foreword, not a 1941 founding editorial; a programme-specific reading remains outstanding.

records.title: New Left Review
records.reason: New Left Review: British intellectual and political context cannot be assigned wholesale to the atlas’s specifically US New Left entry. Review the founding programme and suitability of the research-venue relation.

records.title: Journal of the History of Ideas
records.reason: Journal of the History of Ideas: the existing Cambridge School/contextual-history entry is not an adequate synonym for every history-of-ideas programme. A local search finds no Lovejoy entry or mention. Research the founding programme and broader intellectual-history coverage before creating a target.

records.title: History & Memory
records.reason: History & Memory remains a promising 1989 lead. Its founding programme has not been established in this pass.

records.title: The Public Historian
records.reason: The Public Historian: public history remains a strong dedicated-entry candidate from the 1.112 report; connect existing oral/public-authority, memory and History Workshop coverage.

records.title: Social History of Medicine
records.reason: Social History of Medicine: a dedicated medicine/health field account needs to connect already-present social, scientific, colonial and African-healing approaches.

records.title: Journal of Urban History
records.reason: Journal of Urban History: dedicated urban historiography is a strong candidate, with cities already covered across existing entries.

records.title: Urban History
records.reason: Urban History: preserve the Newsletter/Yearbook/current-title distinctions and do not conflate this journal with Journal of Urban History.

additional_gap_lead.reason: The accepted Holocaust and Genocide Studies programme is broader than the existing Holocaust entry. Inspect comparative genocide content across the atlas before proposing a distinct node.
